experiment.revision_reason: Only the admission scoping changed. The predecessor admitted every node through one alias (probe_node_start with applied_at_start != 0), so each comparison also demanded a result event from nodes that cannot produce that event name and the controller reported 'Admitted operation has no complete applicable result observation' for the admitted nodes without one. The successor emits an explicit per-node mode event - recovery_mode_entered the first time a node shows the install signature, steady_mode_confirmed for the nodes that finish without it - and gives each comparison its own admission alias on that mode event, so admitted operations and result events cover the same node set. Producers, configuration, rounds, command counts, polling density and result event names are unchanged; fresh execution is requested because the comparison basis changed.
experiment.requirement: No InstallSnapshot delivered in this scenario moves a receiver's applied index backwards: a request whose snapshot index is below the receiver's applied state would appear as an applied-index decrease, and a node that entered the install path must keep its applied index monotone just as the nodes that did not.
experiment.responsibility: Receiver-side admission and applied-state bookkeeping of InstallSnapshot (lastApplied set from the request, snapshot index, log store range) observed on nodes that entered the install path and on nodes that did not, within one cluster and one window.

scope.description: One fault-free execution of a normally bootstrapped 3-node in-memory cluster with SnapshotInterval=30ms, SnapshotThreshold=10 and TrailingLogs=5, running three rounds of 25 warm commands, isolating one follower, 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnecting, then 1.2s of polling every 2ms. Identical to the predecessor except for per-node mode admission events.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) with those settings performs real bootstrap, replication, snapshotting and compaction through the in-memory transport.

Isolating one follower leaves the leader with a quorum, so commits continue, the leader compacts past that follower's next index, and the follower recovers through the real InstallSnapshot handler on reconnect.
Two-millisecond polling is dense enough to catch an applied-index decrease, because an install sets lastApplied directly from the request value.
The install signature (snapshot index above the log store last index) marks a node as having entered the install path in this run, which is a mode distinction rather than the measured result.
excluded: Configurations where the leader's latest snapshot index is below a follower's applied index, which this probe does not construct.
Monotonic log store implementations, which take the removeOldLogs branch.
Client-visible consequences of a hypothetical rewind, and any performance measurement.

experiment.prefix: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3, conf) with SnapshotInterval=30ms, SnapshotThreshold=10, TrailingLogs=5 bootstraps the cluster and elects a leader; the harness emits probe_start with the scenario constants and one probe_node_start per node carrying node, is_leader and the starting applied/snapshot/log indices. Three rounds then apply 25 commands through leader.Apply, isolate the lexicographically first follower (c.Disconnect), commit 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnect (c.FullyConnect) and poll all three nodes every 2ms for 1.2s. During polling each node's first observation of the install signature emits recovery_mode_entered with the node, applied index, snapshot index and log store last index at that moment; before the end events, nodes that never showed the signature emit steady_mode_confirmed with the same kind of operands. Per node the harness then emits recovered_node_probe_end or steady_node_probe_end carrying max_applied_seen, applied_at_end, observed_applied_decrease, decrease_count, the prior and new applied index and indices at any decrease, install_signature_ticks, snapshot_index_changes and the end state. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.

comparisons.description: Recovered node: having entered the install path during the rounds, its applied index never moved backwards, so no delivered snapshot was older than its applied state in this execution.

Within-execution comparison: nodes that never entered the install path also kept applied state monotone, so a decrease would have to be attributed to the install path rather than to polling or snapshotting in general.
